title: Bible Composed Challenge
description: Fifteen two-part questions on people, places and teachings across the Bible. Part 1 is the opener; Part 2 is the follow-up on the same story.

questions.question_text: 1. Part 1 — What did God create on the first day?
questions.explanation: Genesis 1:3 records, ‘Let there be light.’

questions.question_text: 1. Part 2 — On which day did God create humankind?
questions.explanation: Genesis 1:26–31 places the creation of humankind on the sixth day.

questions.question_text: 2. Part 1 — Who built the ark?
questions.explanation: Genesis 6–9 tells how Noah built the ark.

questions.question_text: 2. Part 2 — How many of each kind of clean animal did Noah take?
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:2 says Noah took seven pairs of every clean animal.

questions.question_text: 3. Part 1 — Whom did God call to leave his country for a land God would show him?
questions.explanation: Genesis 12 records God’s call to Abram, later named Abraham.

questions.question_text: 3. Part 2 — What was Abraham’s name before God changed it?
questions.explanation: Genesis 17:5 records the change from Abram to Abraham.

questions.question_text: 4. Part 1 — Which of Jacob’s sons was sold into Egypt by his brothers?
questions.explanation: Genesis 37 tells how Joseph was sold and taken to Egypt.

questions.question_text: 4. Part 2 — What office did Joseph later hold in Egypt?
questions.explanation: Pharaoh set Joseph over the land of Egypt (Genesis 41).

questions.question_text: 5. Part 1 — Who led Israel out of Egypt?
questions.explanation: God called Moses to lead the Exodus.

questions.question_text: 5. Part 2 — Which sea did Israel cross on dry ground?
questions.explanation: Exodus 14 describes Israel crossing the Red Sea.

questions.question_text: 6. Part 1 — On which mountain did God give Moses the Ten Commandments?
questions.explanation: Exodus 19–20 places the giving of the law at Mount Sinai.

questions.question_text: 6. Part 2 — How many commandments did God write on the tablets?
questions.explanation: Exodus 20 records the Ten Commandments.

questions.question_text: 7. Part 1 — Which young shepherd defeated Goliath?
questions.explanation: David trusted God and faced Goliath in 1 Samuel 17.

questions.question_text: 7. Part 2 — With what did David strike Goliath?
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 17:49 says David struck Goliath with a stone from his sling.

questions.question_text: 8. Part 1 — Which son of David was known for extraordinary wisdom?
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3 records God granting Solomon outstanding wisdom.

questions.question_text: 8. Part 2 — What famous house of worship did Solomon build in Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 6 describes Solomon building the Temple in Jerusalem.

questions.question_text: 9. Part 1 — Who was thrown into a den of lions for praying to God?
questions.explanation: Daniel 6 records Daniel in the lions’ den.

questions.question_text: 9. Part 2 — Who were the three men thrown into the fiery furnace?
questions.explanation: Daniel 3 names Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego.

questions.question_text: 10. Part 1 — Who was swallowed by a great fish?
questions.explanation: Jonah 1 describes Jonah and the great fish.

questions.question_text: 10. Part 2 — To which city did God send Jonah to preach?
questions.explanation: God sent Jonah to Nineveh (Jonah 1:2).

questions.question_text: 11. Part 1 — Where was Jesus born?
questions.explanation: Matthew 2 and Luke 2 place Jesus’ birth in Bethlehem.

questions.question_text: 11. Part 2 — According to Luke, who first heard that Jesus had been born?
questions.explanation: Luke 2 says angels announced the birth to shepherds.

questions.question_text: 12. Part 1 — How many apostles did Jesus appoint?
questions.explanation: Jesus appointed twelve apostles.

questions.question_text: 12. Part 2 — Which apostle denied Jesus three times before the rooster crowed?
questions.explanation: The Gospels record Peter’s three denials (for example Luke 22).

questions.question_text: 13. Part 1 — In Jesus’ parable, who stopped to help the injured traveller?
questions.explanation: The Good Samaritan showed mercy in Luke 10.

questions.question_text: 13. Part 2 — How many loaves and fish did Jesus use to feed about five thousand people?
questions.option_1: Seven loaves and a few fish
questions.explanation: The Gospels record five loaves and two fish, with twelve baskets left over.

questions.question_text: 14. Part 1 — On which hill was Jesus crucified?
questions.explanation: The Gospels name the place Golgotha, also called Calvary.

questions.question_text: 14. Part 2 — On which day of the week did Jesus rise from the dead?
questions.explanation: The Gospels say Jesus rose on the first day of the week.

questions.question_text: 15. Part 1 — Which book tells about the early church after Jesus’ ascension?
questions.explanation: Acts records the Spirit’s work through the early church.

questions.question_text: 15. Part 2 — What was Paul’s name before his conversion on the road to Damascus?
questions.explanation: Acts 9 records Saul’s conversion; he is later known as Paul.
